newsitem.title: USA: NY Fed's McDonough says CPI best U.S price measure.
newsitem.headline: NY Fed's McDonough says CPI best U.S price measure.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of New York president William McDonough said the Bureau of Labor Statistics' consumer price index (CPI) is the best measure of U.S. inflation despite a general concensus among economists that it overstates price growth.

"We have done a good deal of research at the Federal Reserve and especially at the New York Fed regarding which price indicators are the most reliable and probably the best to guide policy and have come to the conclusion that the core CPI is in fact the best," McDonough said at a conference in New York.
"I believe there is a general agreement (among economists) that there is an (upward) bias," McDonough added, which he calculates between 0.5 and 2.0 percent.
